channel.description: Latest articles from Columbia Journalism Review (cjr.org)

item.title: The Fight over AI at McClatchy
item.description: “Until we have solid language here, we’re not going to feel safe about the integrity of our jobs—or the language our readers read.”

item.title: AI Chatbots Can Search the Web—So Why Don’t They?
item.description: Why AI platforms should be accountable for misrepresenting breaking news

item.title: The Voice in the Deportation Machine
item.description: How Tricia McLaughlin defends Trump’s anti-immigrant agenda.

item.title: S. Mitra Kalita Knows ‘There Is No White Knight Coming to Save Us’
item.description: Five years into supporting outlets that serve communities of color, the cofounder of URL Media talks about the relationship between capitalism and democracy and how nonprofit publishers can operate from a position of power.

item.title: How Politicians and the Press Battle for Eyeballs
item.description: An analysis of politicians’ official social media accounts.

item.title: A Veteran of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette—and Its Long Strike—Prepares for What’s Next
item.description: “We didn’t go on strike to put the paper out of business. We went on strike to keep it good.”

item.title: The Word Out
item.description: Courageous reporting from Minnesota and Iran. Plus: tone-deafness at the Tribune; spit hoods in Seattle.

item.title: The Astonishing Arrests of Don Lemon and Georgia Fort
item.description: In an interview, Fort described a challenge in her work documenting news in the Twin Cities: “Every independent journalist is kind of every person for themselves.” Two days later, officers came to her door.

item.title: ‘I Might Get Arrested, People’
item.description: How MAGA media outlets are fueling Trump’s crackdown on the press.

item.title: Shayan Sardarizadeh on Identifying the Victims of Iran’s Deadly Protest Crackdown
item.description: “We do it so that people in the general public don’t have to.”
